items.description: The Supreme Court had ordered that Imran Khan be kept in the hospital till the next hearing on Sept. 16; however, he was taken to the state-run PIMS in Islamabad during the night of August 20-21 for medical examination and treatment before being returned to Adiala Jail

items.title: Zhou Bo: China’s alternative to Western power
items.description: Senior Colonel Zhou Bo and Sreenivasan Jain discuss China's vision of a fairer, multipolar world and work towards that.

items.description: Authorities said the fire was caused by humans.

items.title: USA and China at war over Vaca Muerta, Hidrovía and Patagonia
items.description: Dispute between Washington and Beijing for global technological influence is alive in Argentina. Huawei lies at the centre of the controversy due to its participation in CALF projects in Neuquén, while the United States demands “networks of confidence” to protect data linked to Vaca Muerta. items.title: Duck brigade replaces pesticides on wine farm in South Africa
items.description: Indian runner ducks are used, alongside sheep and cattle, at Vergenoegd Löw to control insects and trim down crops and weeds in the vineyards.

items.title: Kazakhstan's future after the elections: Russia, EU or China
items.description: Kazakhstan, where power is being continuously consolidated in the president's hands, will have to continue its tough balancing act between the EU, Russia and China following the parliamentary elections this Sunday.

items.title: Australia confirms H5N1 bird flu case in local mammal
items.description: Australian authorities said the deadly virus's spread to mammals was "concerning" but "not unexpected."

items.title: Kejelcha breaks men's half marathon world record by 29 seconds

items.description: Nancy Kassebaum Baker was elected to the U.S. Senate in 1978 and served three terms

items.title: Central African Republic shuts Zamboye gold mine after deadly collapse
items.description: Authorities in the Central African Republic have closed an artisanal gold mine near the Cameroon border after a landslide killed at least 49 people, according to the official toll. Local sources say the death toll could be around 100, with many miners still missing.

items.title: Transshipment scam or efficient supply chain? How U.S. firms turn it into profit?

items.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy rejects wartime elections
items.description: The Ukrainian president says wartime elections, as called for by the ex-defense minister, could "split Ukraine." He also said Russia was planning to mobilize hundreds of thousands of troops after September polls there.

items.title: Harry Kane named footballer of the year in Germany
items.description: Harry Kane has added another honor after a remarkable season for Bayern Munich and a strong World Cup with England. Bayern also took the top prize in coaching, and the club's Giulia Gwinn won women's Player of the Year.

items.title: Video: Thousands of families flee fighting in Sudan’s North Kordofan State
items.description: Mothers and their children are in dire need of food and safety in Sudan’s conflict-stricken Kordofan State.

items.title: Surging unemployment is Milei’s biggest political threat in Argentina
items.description: For a second straight year, the economy is growing yet employment is falling in the formal sector. Only one province, Neuquén, has added businesses during Milei’s tenure. Leer más

items.title: Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan sentenced to life in prison
items.description: A Chinese court ordered the former billionaire's assets to be confiscated and fined Evergrande-related companies billions of dollars.

items.title: DEA chief calls Argentina a 'model' for region in anti-narco fight

items.title: Iran executes man accused of aiding U.S., Israel in anti-government protests

items.title: Police summon Zambian opposition leader for questioning after disputed vote
items.description: Zambian opposition leader Brian Mundubile has been summoned for questioning by police over an alleged national security threat. Mundubile lost to incumbent Hakainde Hichilema in last week's presidential election and has vowed to challenge the results in court.

items.title: Wartime elections would 'destroy' Ukraine, says Zelensky
items.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said in remarks made public Sunday that wartime elections would be a "tsunami" that would "destroy the country". Kyiv has been engulfed in a political crisis over the summer, triggered when Zelensky fired popular defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who days later called to organise a vote.

items.title: As they return to the UK, Harry and Meghan search for a brand that sticks
items.description: They will not be working royals when they come back. So what could they be doing instead?

items.title: 'Quiet, quiet, quiet!'
items.description: As the US president insults a journalist again, the BBC looks at the questions he does not like to answer.
items.source: What triggers Trump to shut down reporters?

items.title: Venezuela: Two months after the quake, 12,500 people still live in temporary camps
items.description: Two months after two earthquakes struck Venezuela, more than 12,500 people are still living in temporary camps in La Guaira. Many survivors are still struggling to come to terms with the loss of loved ones and their homes. They have been forced to adapt to precarious living conditions, exposed to the elements, with little access to medical care and humanitarian aid. France 24 reporters Herminia Fernández and Julio Uribarris visited three camps housing earthquake survivors.

items.title: Guinea-Bissau opposition calls for boycott of constitutional referendum
items.description: Guinea-Bissau’s opposition PAIGC is calling for a boycott of the country’s upcoming constitutional referendum, citing fears of rigged vote.

items.title: US military newspaper editor voices censorship fears after being fired
items.description: Erik Slavin believes he was fired for saying in an interview that "in a hypothetical situation, censorship would be a red line".

items.title: Belgian university suspends academic who accused Arday of plagiarism
items.description: Researcher Nathan Cofnas said in a post on X that he was under investigation by Ghent University for "discriminating" against the late Cambridge professor.

items.title: Ethiopia: Tigrayan women celebrate Ashenda amid fears of new war
items.description: In Addis Ababa, Tigrayan women gather to celebrate Ashenda, while expressing hopes for lasting peace in Ethiopia's Tigray region, where recent drone strikes on the regional capital Mekella have renewed fears of conflict after the devastating 2020-2022 war

items.title: Nigeria: Jihadis kidnap dozens during Friday prayers
items.description: Witnesses said men carrying guns and machetes set upon two villages in Niger State. Many details about the attack have yet to be confirmed by police.

items.title: Trump hits out at Canada over retaliatory tariffs
items.description: Donald Trump has accused Canada of treating US farmers unfairly for years as a trade standoff between Ottawa and Washington escalates. Both sides are threatening new tariffs after the collapse of talks on Friday.

items.title: City's drinking water diluted after elevated PFAS levels detected
items.description: Riverina Water is diluting water from two of its Wagga Wagga bores due to elevated levels of so-called "forever chemicals" being detected, but the source of contamination is a mystery.

items.title: Indonesian police arrest 72 people suspected of starting forest fires
items.description: The arson suspects were being investigated in connection with 89 forest and land fire cases across five provinces on the island of Borneo and four on Sumatra, said Mohammad Irhamni, director of special crimes at the National Police's Criminal Investigation Agency

items.title: Hundreds of Gaza children join a mass swimming lesson to cope with trauma
items.description: In Gaza, the war has upended the lives of an entire generation of children. In an effort to help them cope with the trauma of the conflict, an NGO has launched a project in Khan Younis: a huge swimming lesson that could even set a world record. Hundreds of children have gathered on the beach to learn how to swim. Story by Charlotte Hughes.
